flags.note: The שֶׁ + perfect construction for attributive relative clause is standard Mishnaic Hebrew, but the specific syntax here mirrors Greek participial structure rather than natural Hebrew flow.
The שֶׁ + imperfect construction translating Greek τὰ δεῖ γενέσθαι ('what must come to pass') shows Greek influence in the temporal/modal nuance.
The מי שֶׁ construction is acceptable in Hebrew, but the participle מאמין here follows Greek participial usage rather than typical Hebrew verbal syntax.
The מה שֶׁ + passive participle construction mirrors Greek articular participle τὰ γεγραμμένα rather than natural Hebrew expression.
The שֶׁ relative with hif'il perfect follows Greek participial structure more than natural Hebrew relative clause construction.

flags.hebrew: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ רַע תִּהְיֶה כָּל עֵת כָּךְ
flags.note: This construction with repeated מי שיש + predicate adjective + jussive is extremely awkward in Hebrew and clearly translates Greek ὁ ἀδικῶν ἀδικησάτω ἔτι structure.
The repetitive parallel structure with כך and גם כן shows Greek influence from the fourfold parallel construction in the Greek text.
The purpose clause with כדי שֶׁ + imperfect translating Greek ἵνα shows Greek syntactic influence on Hebrew purpose expression.
The parallel מי שֶׁ constructions with present-tense meaning mirror Greek ὁ ἀκούων... ὁ διψῶν participial structure.

flags.hebrew: וּבְאִם שֶׁאֶחָד יוֹסִיף לוֹ אֵיזֶה דְּבָרִים
flags.note: The conditional structure with ובאם שאחד + future + object pronoun + indefinite object mirrors Greek ἐάν τις ἐπιθῇ ἐπ' αὐτὰ word order rather than natural Hebrew syntax.

flags.hebrew: וּבְאִם שֶׁאֶחָד יִגְרַע אֵיזֶה דְּבָרִים מִזֶּה הַסֵּפֶר
